meta.triageRationale: A single cohesive UX rework of one existing panel (renderRepoConfig), with a real design decision (how to group 34 roles, how to implement collapsible sections in a VS-Code-free HTML string renderer plus the shared webview bootstrap script) and multiple build tasks (renderer restructure, CSS, bootstrap-script toggle wiring, tests). Not trivial/small since it touches the renderer logic, the shared shellHtml CSS block, and the webview-host.ts bootstrap script together (the same multi-file shape as the just-completed Model Tiers Story, which was also sized 'feature'). Not an epic: no new subsystem, no new top-level module — it reworks the presentation of an existing, already-shipped panel (Story E20260923401ae5fb:S007) without touching its write path, data model, or daemon contract.

findings.premise: The design covers the full stated intent (group role rows by criticality into collapsible sections, separate core-floor section, status-card Providers) and builds nothing from the mock's declared non-goals ('Show N more' truncation, custom .chev indicator).
findings.evidence: mocks/repo-config-grouped.html's caption lists three open questions for round 2, including the client-JS toggle and 'show N more'. The LLD Summary explicitly resolves the client-JS question (native <details>/<summary>, no script) and declares both truncation and the .chev element as non-goals, consistent with alternative a1 in section 7.1 which is chosen specifically because it needs no new script. Section 2.1's postconditions and the Migration section's steps (1-3) only add grouping/section CSS and reshape two render functions — no truncation or chevron code is specified anywhere in the Data model, Error paths, Test strategy, or Migration sections.
findings.action: none — coverage matches stated scope and the explicit non-goals are honored throughout.

findings.premise: Today renderRepoConfig renders one flat <table class="role-tiers"> of all roles, a separate <table class="core-floor">, and renderProvidersSection renders three distinct checkbox-label variants, with no grouping beyond <h3> headers, exactly as the Migration 'State before' and references c1/c3 describe.

summary.prose: This Story reworks the VS Code Repo Configuration panel's presentation: the flat 34-row role-tiers table becomes two collapsible groups (Critical, open by default; Peripheral, collapsed) split on the existing RoleDescriptor.criticality field, the core floor gets its own section, and the Providers checkbox list becomes status-card rows (registered / not registered / CLI unavailable) — delivering the same grouping/collapse behavior the approved mock at mocks/repo-config-grouped.html demonstrates, via native <details>/<summary> disclosure (resolving the mock's own open question about client-side JS: none is needed) rather than the mock's own div+.collapsed+.chev markup. No write path, message shape, or daemon capability changes; this is a presentation-only rework of the already-shipped Story S007 panel. Non-goals: (1) the mock's 'Show N more' truncation inside an expanded group (left as an explicit open question for round 2 in the mock's own caption) is NOT implemented by this Story — a1's win over a2 was specifically that it needs no new client-side script, and truncation would require one; an expanded group always renders its full role list. (2) the mock's custom .chev indicator is NOT reproduced — the native <summary> disclosure triangle is the sole expand/collapse indicator, so no separate chevron element risks doubling up with it.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Group the Repo Configuration panel's role tiers by criticality, with status-card Providers

api.name: renderRepoConfig

returns.meaning: unchanged (selected) => Promise<string> shape; the returned HTML now groups role rows into two <details> sections (open=Critical, closed=Peripheral) instead of one flat <table class="role-tiers">, delivering the same grouping/collapse behavior the approved mock at mocks/repo-config-grouped.html demonstrates — via native <details>/<summary>, not the mock's own div+.collapsed+.chev markup

preconditions: same as today: registeredRepos()/rawConfig() rejections propagate unchanged (uncaught, bubbling to the host's renderRepoPanel try/catch); mcpRegistration() rejections are instead caught LOCALLY inside renderRepoConfig (repo-config.ts:120-129) and degrade to an in-section hint paragraph, never propagating — these are two different behaviors, not one

the native <summary> disclosure triangle is the ONLY expand/collapse indicator — no separate .chev element is rendered, so there is no risk of a double indicator; only its color/size may be restyled via the summary::marker pseudo-element
core floor keeps its own <section>, visually separated from the role groups (was already its own <table> today; now styled as its own section like the role groups)
no change to which segments a field write addresses (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:52-55's isRepoModelWrite is untouched)

dataModelChanges.details: A local (module-private, not exported) grouping shape built inside renderRepoConfig: { criticality: Criticality; label: string; roles: readonly RoleDescriptor[] }. Criticality is the existing type from role-taxonomy.ts; this is purely an internal rendering grouping, not a new daemon or config shape.

errorCases.scenario: A future third Criticality value is added to role-taxonomy.ts without updating the grouping logic in renderRepoConfig.
errorCases.detection: TypeScript's exhaustiveness checking on the closed 'critical'|'peripheral' union (Criticality, role-taxonomy.ts) fails to compile if the grouping switch/partition does not handle every member — caught at build time (npx tsc --noEmit), not at runtime.
errorCases.response: The grouping code must be written as an exhaustive switch/partition over Criticality so a new member is a compile error, not a silently-dropped role.
errorCases.userImpact: None in practice — this is a build-time guard, not a runtime failure a user would ever see.

errorCases.scenario: registeredRepos() / rawConfig() rejects while rendering the grouped panel.
errorCases.detection: Same as today: the await inside renderRepoConfig's async body rejects (uncaught at this level).
errorCases.response: Unchanged — the rejection propagates to the host's existing never-throw wrapper (renderRepoPanel's try/catch in webview-host.ts), which degrades to the existing error body. No new error handling is added or needed for the regroup.
errorCases.userImpact: Unchanged from today: an in-panel error state instead of the form.

errorCases.scenario: mcpRegistration() rejects while rendering the Providers section.
errorCases.detection: Same as today: repo-config.ts:120-129's own local try/catch around `await deps.mcpRegistration()` catches the rejection — it never reaches renderRepoConfig's outer scope.
errorCases.response: Unchanged — the catch renders an in-section hint paragraph (an 'unknown method' update prompt when the message matches /unknown method/, else a generic unavailability hint) in place of the Providers list; the rest of the panel (role groups, core floor) still renders normally. This is a DIFFERENT behavior from the registeredRepos()/rawConfig() case: it does not propagate and does not degrade the whole panel.
errorCases.userImpact: The Providers section shows a hint instead of the provider list; the role-tier groups and core floor remain fully usable.

edgeCases.input: A repo with every role and the core floor left at 'global' (no overrides at all).
edgeCases.expected: Both groups still render all 34 rows (14 critical + 20 peripheral) each showing 'global' selected; grouping is independent of whether any override exists.

edgeCases.input: Every known provider is either already registered or unavailable (none checkable).
edgeCases.expected: Every provider renders as a non-checkable status card (registered or CLI-unavailable chip); the 'Register selected providers' button is omitted, exactly as today's checkable-count check already does.

edgeCases.input: The user switches the selected repo (a fresh selectRepo re-render).
edgeCases.expected: The new document's <details> elements reset to their markup-declared default state (critical open, peripheral closed) — a previously-expanded peripheral group does not persist across a repo switch, since each render is a fresh HTML document with no client-side state carried over.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A field write addresses only ['tasks', roleId] or ['coreFloor'] segments — the grouped/card presentation changes no write-path segment shape.

A registeredRepos()/rawConfig() rejection propagates to the host's existing never-throw degrade path, unchanged by the regroup; an mcpRegistration() rejection is instead caught locally inside renderRepoConfig and degrades only the Providers section — these two distinct behaviors are both preserved unchanged.

The checkable provider input's data-provider attribute and REPO_BOOTSTRAP's querySelectorAll('input[data-provider]') collection for the Register button are preserved exactly — the status-card rework does not touch the registration message flow.
All 34 roles (14 critical + 20 peripheral, per reasoningRoleTaxonomy().roles) continue to render somewhere in the grouped output — none silently dropped by the criticality partition.

migration.stateBefore: renderRepoConfig renders one flat <table class="role-tiers"> with all 34 roles as plain <tr> rows (no grouping), one <table class="core-floor"> row, and renderProvidersSection renders a flat list of three different <label><input></label> checkbox variants — no visual structure beyond <h3> section headers (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:131-139).
migration.stateAfter: renderRepoConfig renders role rows split into two <details class="section"> groups by criticality (Critical open by default, Peripheral closed), the core floor in its own section, and renderProvidersSection renders status-card rows (registered / not registered / CLI-unavailable chips) — delivering the same grouping/collapse behavior as mocks/repo-config-grouped.html via native <details>/<summary> rather than its div+.collapsed+.chev markup. The write path, message shapes, and daemon reads are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the new .section/.section-head/.count/.rows/.role-row/.provider-row/.status-chip/.floor-row CSS rules to webview-host.ts's shared shellHtml style block, additive to the existing .tier/.note/.hosting-chip rules the Model Tiers Story already added there. Unlike the mock, no .chev/.collapsed rules are needed (native <details>/<summary> provides its own disclosure marker and open/closed state); optionally restyle the marker's color via the summary::marker pseudo-element.

Rewrite renderRepoConfig to partition reasoningRoleTaxonomy().roles by criticality into two RoleGroup values and render each as a <details> section via the reshaped tierRow; give the core floor its own section wrapper.
Rewrite renderProvidersSection to render status-card rows instead of the three checkbox-label variants, preserving the checkable data-provider input exactly where it exists today.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API signature changes: renderRepoConfig/createRepoConfigWriteHandler/createRepoRegisterProvidersHandler keep their existing exported signatures. tierRow and renderProvidersSection are module-private helpers, so their internal markup reshape is not a breaking change to any consumer. The webview->host message shapes (selectRepo/repoWrite/repoRegisterProviders) and the write-path segment validation (isRepoModelWrite) are untouched.

alternativesConsidered.name: Native <details>/<summary> collapsible sections
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Render each role group as a standard HTML5 <details> element (open by default for Critical, closed for Peripheral) with no new client-side script.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
renderRepoConfig emits
Critical roles 14
...
for the critical group and the same without open for peripheral. The browser's native disclosure behavior handles expand/collapse; no postMessage, no REPO_BOOTSTRAP change. Providers becomes a
of status-card rows replacing the three checkbox label variants.
pros: Zero new webview->host message, zero REPO_BOOTSTRAP change
Native, accessible disclosure semantics for free
cons: <details>'s native marker is harder to restyle pixel-for-pixel to the mock's custom glyph
No 'show N more' truncation inside an open group without extra markup/script

alternativesConsidered.name: Custom div sections with a REPO_BOOTSTRAP click-toggle
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Reproduce the mock's exact .section/.section-head/.collapsed markup, with a new click listener in REPO_BOOTSTRAP toggling a 'collapsed' class.
alternativesConsidered.approach: renderRepoConfig emits plain div-based section markup matching the mock verbatim; REPO_BOOTSTRAP gains a new listener toggling .collapsed — a local DOM class flip, no postMessage.
pros: Pixel-exact match to the approved mock
Full control over a future 'show N more' truncation
cons: Adds a new script listener for a purely cosmetic effect <details> already provides natively
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 but costs more (a new script listener) for a purely cosmetic gain (pixel-exact chevron) — fails the smallest-complete-change constraint a1 satisfies.

alternativesConsidered.name: Grouped but always-expanded (no collapse)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep both groups visually separated but always fully expanded — drop the collapse/expand interaction entirely.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same two-group split and status-card Providers as a1/a2, but render both groups always expanded with no <details>/no toggle.
pros: Simplest possible markup, no collapse state to reason about
cons: Drops the exact behavior the approved mock demonstrates (peripheral collapsed by default)
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest, but fails the collapse-behavior constraint outright — the user explicitly approved a mock whose entire point was hiding the 20-role peripheral group by default; always-expanded reintroduces the problem the Story exists to solve.
